history.period: Present complex from the 1970s; legend from the Kalika Purana
history.summary: POSSIBLE CSV DUPLICATE of seq 1263 (Parshuram Kund) — the Devi Renuka shrine is a sub-shrine inside the Parshuram Kund temple complex, not an independent site; merge-or-drop decision needed. It is dedicated to Devi Renuka, mother of Parashurama. Local legend holds that at Maharishi Jamadagni's command Parashurama beheaded his mother Renuka with his axe, then asked for her life back as his boon, and she was revived; another telling says she leapt into the Lohit to escape King Sahastrabahu. The shrine is reached by climbing the temple steps above the kund; all travel, festival and access details are the same as for Parshuram Kund (seq 1263). CSV town 'Parasuram Kund' is the site name; nearest town Wakro (16 km).

name: Devi Renuka Shrine
town_description: Wakro is a small town in Lohit district at the foothills of the Mishmi Hills, about 16 km from Parshuram Kund. It is the nearest market town and the last roadhead before the pilgrimage site, lying close to the Kamlang Reserve Forest.

travel.railway: New Tinsukia Junction, Assam, about 151 km
travel.road: About 48 km from Tezu and 16 km from Wakro; state-run and private buses and taxis run from Tinsukia, Dibrugarh and Tezu

visitor_information.best_time: January for the Makar Sankranti mela; more generally October to March (winter)
visitor_information.opening_hours: Daylight hours with the Parshuram Kund complex; an entry permit is required — issued at Dirak and Sunpura check posts during the mela
